artists.biography: Kurt Vile (born 1980 in Philadelphia) is an American guitarist and singer. Previously the lead guitarist in the band The War on Drugs, he began his solo career in 2008.  Vile began his musical career in 2003 creating lo-fi home recordings with frequent collaborator Adam Granduciel. The duo subsequently formed the indie rock band The War on Drugs in 2005. Vile departed following the release of their debut studio album, Wagonwheel Blues, in 2008.  Vile's music has been likened to Bruce Springsteen, Bob Seger, and Tom Petty. His first album for Matador, titled Childish Prodigy was released in October 2009. Prior to signing with Matador, Vile released two albums, God is Saying This to You and Constant Hitmaker, on Mexican Summer and Woodsist, respectively. He plays both solo shows as well as shows with a backing band called The Violators.  Smoke Ring For My Halo, released in March of 2011, is Kurt Vile's fourth album and second official release for Matador Records. Uncut placed the album at number 14 on its list of "Top 50 albums of 2011" and garnered Vile the iTunes #Rewind2011 Singer/Songwriter Album of the Year. Vile followed up the widely acclaimed album with the six-song EP release, So Outta Reach, in November of the same year. The EP was composed of tracks originating from the same sessions that birthed Smoke Ring for My Halo. So Outta Reach includes the single 'The Creature', acknowledged as one of Vile's best, and a driving rock cover of Bruce Springsteen's 'Downbound Train'.

perplexity.description:
Kurt Vile’s Bottle It In, released in 2018 on Matador Records, is a sprawling, introspective rock album that showcases Vile’s signature blend of laid-back guitar work, meandering song structures, and wry, self-deprecating lyrics. The album’s sound is rooted in psychedelic and indie rock, with elements of folk and country woven throughout, creating a relaxed yet intricate sonic landscape. Standout tracks like “Loading Zones,” “Bassackwards,” and “Come Again” highlight Vile’s knack for crafting melodic, guitar-driven songs that balance spontaneity with meticulous production.

Bottle It In marks a significant point in Vile’s discography, following his breakthrough success with Wakin on a Pretty Daze and the hit single “Pretty Pimpin’.” The album further solidified his reputation as a leading figure in contemporary indie rock, praised for its ambitious scope and emotional depth. Critics lauded the album for its cohesive yet adventurous approach, with many noting its expansive runtime and the subtle evolution of Vile’s songwriting. Commercially, Bottle It In received strong reviews and performed well on alternative charts, affirming Vile’s status as a critically acclaimed and influential artist within the genre.
